newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks continue upward march on Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks continue upward march on Q2 earnings.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued their early advance to post strong gains at midday dealing on Thursday on what dealers said was a moderate but steady stream of buyers encouraged by earnings reports.
"Second quarter earnings are going down well. We don't have a flood of buyers, but investors are stepping in," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 57.29 points, or 1.21 percent, at 4,799.41.
Trading volume was restrained at 53.1 million shares.
"Volume is neither good nor bad, but a little low-key. Players still seem a little shaken after last week's volatility on Brazil," the trader added.
Dealers said investors had become more enthusiastic over earnings posted late on Tuesday by market heavyweight Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which was driving the market.

Telmex, which accounted for one-fifth of all shares dealt, was up 52 centavos to 20.40 pesos in Mexico while its ADRs continued to shrug off losses on Wall Street to stand up 1-1/4 at 52. The Dow Jones was off 44.37 points at 8,043.99.

Dealers said food company Grupo Corvi and retailer Controladora Comercial Mexicana (Comerci) had gained strongly in relatively brisk trade on expectations they would post favorable second quarter earnings.
Corvi UBL shares were up 33 centavos to 5.20 pesos, while Comerci had gained 36 centavos to 8.00 pesos.
On the broad market, gainers outpaced sliders by 56 to 30 out of 105 stocks traded.
